title: Pseudoreplication and the Design of Ecological Field Experiments
authors: Hurlbert, S. H.
notes: Canonical statement of the failure mode this repository independently rejected as REJ-COHORT-05: treating non-independent replicates as independent inflates the false-positive rate. The rejection of the N=40 pseudoreplicated cohort and the move to disjoint N=100 cohorts matches the standard remedy (independent experimental units). Cite as vindication of that decision, not as an endorsement of the analysis.

title: A Practitioner's Guide to Cluster-Robust Inference
authors: Cameron, A. C.; Miller, D. L.
notes: Supplies the correct inferential frame for the paired ablation design: seeds are clusters, and the paired within-seed contrast is the estimation target. Relevant caveat the repository does not currently state: with ~40-100 clusters the wild cluster bootstrap is preferred over the percentile bootstrap, and with fewer than ~10 clusters the six-point (Webb) weight distribution becomes necessary. Round 1 did not verify which bootstrap variant `AIEF_1_3_paired_statistics_updated.py` uses beyond its 95% percentile interval claim; that is a Round 2 audit item.

title: Nonlinear normal modes and spectral submanifolds: existence, uniqueness and use in model reduction
authors: Haller, G.; Ponsioen, S.
notes: Gives the precise sense in which REJ-SPEC-01 was doomed: an exact slow reduction requires an invariant manifold tangent to a spectral subspace, not a truncated POD basis. The rejected 8D compression assumed a finite-dimensional invariant subspace it never established. This is the strongest external justification for the REJ-SPEC-01 rejection in the current record.

title: Data-Driven Reduced Modeling of Delayed Dynamical Systems via Spectral Submanifolds
authors: Abbasciano, G.; Buza, G.; Haller, G.
notes: Highest-priority find of Round 1. This is the direct methodological competitor to the rejected POD compression and the correct framework for the AIEF-1.4 delay system: it reduces a DDE to a low-dimensional ODE model without knowing the delay structure, and reports predictive power retained under chaos. Two consequences. (1) REJ-SPEC-01 is not merely a coding error; a sound delay-aware reduction exists and was not attempted. (2) A future AIEF-1.4 spectral program has a published, citable target to reproduce or beat, instead of an internally invented baseline.

title: Data-driven discovery of Koopman eigenfunctions for control
authors: Kaiser, E.; Kutz, J. N.; Brunton, B. W.
notes: Names the closure/aliasing failure that produces plausible-looking but spurious eigenvalues in exactly the regime REJ-SPEC-01 occupied. Usable as the formal justification that an 8D projected operator's spectrum is not automatically attributable to the full system.

title: Avoiding spectral pollution for transfer operators using residuals
authors: Herwig, A.; Colbrook, M. J.; Junge, O.; Koltai, P.; Slipantschuk, J.
notes: Supplies the residual-based (ResDMD-style) acceptance test the rejected spectral program lacked: an eigenpair is only admissible if its residual against the full dynamics is small. This is directly implementable as a gate on any future slow-mode claim and would have caught REJ-SPEC-01 automatically. Round 2 action item: specify the residual threshold that AIEF-1.4 slow modes must satisfy.

title: Koopman Reduced Order Modeling with Confidence Bounds
authors: Mohr, R.; Fonoberova, M.; Mezic, I.
notes: The constructive alternative to the rejected compression: truncating the spectrum is only defensible if the discarded remainder is carried as an explicit error process with bounds. AIEF-1.4 truncation carried no such term, so 'faithfully captures' in REJ-SPEC-01 had no quantitative referent. Gives a template for stating a bounded claim instead of a qualitative one.

title: Spectra and Pseudospectra: The Behavior of Nonnormal Matrices and Operators
authors: Trefethen, L. N.; Embree, M.
notes: Frames CAVEAT-MS-8.4 and CF08 correctly. When the finite-step operator is non-normal, left and right eigenvectors are not orthogonal and the pointwise left-covector decomposition is not an invariant object; it is a property of one fiber/eigenvector normalization. The draft Corollary 8.4 defect (the extra diag(x_G) C_G term) is the concrete instance. Round 2 action item: compute the pseudospectrum radius of the audited AIEF-1.4 operator at eps=1e-8 to state the tie-margin claim in Trefethen-Embree terms rather than as an ad hoc tolerance.

title: Optimization and Nonsmooth Analysis
authors: Clarke, F. H.
notes: The map A_eps(x) = M(Ax)x with min()-selected endpoint winners is piecewise-smooth and generally not differentiable at winner ties, which is exactly the regime REJ-SPEC-02 and S04 (the t=124.05 'event') live in. Clarke's generalized gradient is the standard object of record there. This converts an unexplained sensitivity into a named mathematical condition: at a tie the branchwise Jacobian does not exist and a directional/generalized derivative must be reported instead.

title: Introduction to Functional Differential Equations
authors: Hale, J. K.; Verduyn Lunel, S. M.
notes: Formal license for the repository's central structural claim: for a delay system the state is the history segment x_t, so 'memory' is not an extra feature but part of the state space. This is why EMP-AIEF14-01 (reset_B is not a unique bottleneck) is unsurprising rather than paradoxical: removing one component of a history-dependent state leaves the history itself intact.

title: Algebraic Graph Theory
authors: Godsil, C.; Royle, G.
notes: Anchors LEAN-CF-01 in the literature. ker C_{2,7} = span{(1,-1,-1)} is the n-c instance for the 2-vertex/3-edge multigraph with c=1: rank = n - c = 1, so nullity = 3 - 1 = 2 in edge coordinates, and the Lean statement is the specific orientation-compatible computation. The Lean result is therefore a correct specialization of a classical theorem, which is the right status: formalized theorem, not new mathematics.

title: Parallel Reproducible Summation
authors: Demmel, J.; Nguyen, H. D.
notes: Bounds what IMPL-MODULAR-01 can honestly claim. Bit-identical agreement is a same-order, same-environment property; it is not guaranteed across architectures, compilers, libm versions or thread counts. The observed cross-host drift (4.405e-13 on continuous arrays, 0.0 on discrete P_* arrays) is the textbook behaviour, not a defect. IMPL-MODULAR-01 is correctly scoped to 'identical host/libm environment' already; this reference is what makes that scope boundary citable rather than merely cautious.

title: Algorithms for Efficient Reproducible Floating Point Summation
authors: Ahrens, W.; Demmel, J.; Nguyen, H. D.
notes: Actionable if the project ever wants cross-platform bitwise reproducibility rather than tolerance-gated reproducibility. Round 2/3 candidate: specify the two-tier tolerance gate for Stage 7 CI (0.0 on discrete P_* arrays; a justified absolute tolerance for continuous DDE arrays) and cite this as the reason a 0-ULP gate is not attainable by default.

title: What every computer scientist should know about floating-point arithmetic
authors: Goldberg, D.
notes: Baseline reference for two separate repo findings. (a) The eps=1e-8 finite-difference Jacobian in REJ-SPEC-02 is two to three orders of magnitude larger than the 4.44e-14 tie margins it was meant to resolve, so the reported spectrum is dominated by the difference step, not the dynamics. (b) The 4.405e-13 cross-host drift is at the rounding-error scale the tutorial predicts. Both are now citable rather than asserted.

title: Network Motifs: Simple Building Blocks of Complex Networks
authors: Milo, R.; Shen-Orr, S.; Itzkovitz, S.; Kashtan, N.; Chklovskii, D.; Alon, U.
notes: Defines the standard the rejected K3 census did not meet. 'Motif' is a statement about excess over a degree-matched null ensemble, never a raw count. REJ-K3-04 reported 856 K3 instances and inferred dominance; the correct comparison is against a configuration-model ensemble at matched degree sequence, and the audit already found only 26 isolated K3 components. Round 2 action item: specify the null model and rewiring count needed to restate any K3 claim as a z-score.

title: Network Attractors driven by Time-Delay Plasticity
authors: Ruschel, S.; Hristov, E.; Meijer, H. G. E.; Coombes, S.; Nicks, R.
notes: Closest published neighbour to the AIEF-1.4 memory/timescale programme: adaptive delays that reshape effective coupling, select frequencies, and stabilise network attractors. Two uses. (1) Priority/scoop risk: EMP-AIEF14-02 is a specific instance of a mechanism now under independent investigation, so the repository should state the novelty boundary explicitly (its contributions are the ablation design and the topological-recovery metric, not the existence of delay-driven frequency selection). (2) Benchmark: the AAD literature has an algebraic frequency-selection picture, which is a stricter standard than a numerically observed T_window sensitivity.

title: The Multiverse of Dynamic Mode Decomposition Algorithms
authors: Colbrook, M. J.
notes: Resolves LEAD-0001, and corrects it: the review is by a single author, not a group. It is the standard map of DMD-as-spectral-computation, with a three-way taxonomy (linear-regression, Galerkin, structure-preserving) and a MATLAB package. Relevant because the rejected 8D compression used one regression variant with no convergence argument; this review is the catalogue of what else was available and is the correct entry point for any future attempt.

title: Synchronization and resilience in the Kuramoto white matter network model with adaptive state-dependent delays
authors: Park, S. H.; Lefebvre, J.
notes: Resolves LEAD-0002: Park & Lefebvre, not an anonymous group. This is the earliest verified member of the adaptive-delay cluster (2020), predating LIT-0016 and LIT-0028. One sentence in the paper is structurally important and was not in the Round 1 record: the model 'corresponds to an N + N^2-dimensional functional differential equation with state-dependent delays'. The state dimension grows with the edge set. That is the concrete reason EMP-AIEF14-01 (no single component is a privileged memory bottleneck) is expected rather than surprising - it is the same argument as LIT-0010, now with an explicit dimension count.

title: Random Dynamical Systems
authors: Arnold, L.
notes: Resolves LEAD-0003 and fills domain L4, which Round 1 left entirely empty. This is the primary reference for the cocycle formalism the repository invokes. IMPORTANT OPEN ITEM: a cocycle is not a naming preference, it is an identity - Phi(t+s, w) = Phi(t, theta_s w) Phi(s, w) over a measure-preserving shift theta. Round 2 did NOT verify that the construction called the 'history cocycle' in AIEF_1_4_TANGENT_AND_COCYCLE satisfies that composition law. Flagged as a Round 3 verification item, because if it does not, the claim needs a different word.

title: Piecewise-smooth Dynamical Systems: Theory and Applications
authors: di Bernardo, M.; Budd, C. J.; Champneys, A. R.; Kowalczyk, P.
notes: The framing reference for the entire CF01-CF12 block, which Round 1 left with no literature at all. The admissibility map A_eps(x) = M(Ax)x with min-selected endpoint winners is piecewise-smooth; this book is the standard treatment of that class. Consequence for S04: the 'event' at t=124.05 is a discontinuity-induced phenomenon, not an implementation defect, and the book supplies the vocabulary (border collision / boundary-equilibrium bifurcation) to say precisely which.

title: Lexicographic differentiation of nonsmooth functions
authors: Nesterov, Yu.
notes: Supplies the uniqueness theorem behind CF03. Once a basis is fixed, the lexicographic derivative is unique - which is exactly the property needed at winner ties, and exactly the property a branchwise Jacobian does not have. Note the paper's own claim that the lexicographic subdifferential is *more* rigorous than Clarke's: for the CF block, lexicographic differentiation is the stronger tool, not a fallback when Clarke is inconvenient.

title: A vector forward mode of automatic differentiation for generalized derivative evaluation
authors: Khan, K. A.; Barton, P. I.
notes: The implementable bridge between LIT-0021 and the code. It gives an automatic-differentiation forward mode for lexicographic directional derivatives, with rules for min, max, mid and abs - and AIEF's winner map is built from min(). So the exact nontrivial primitive the audit needed is covered by an existing method. Second, useful negative evidence: the approach explicitly treats finite differencing as unsuitable for nonsmooth functions ('stepping' over nonsmooth points), which is the formal statement of why REJ-SPEC-02 could not be rescued by shrinking epsilon.

title: Investigating Causal Relations by Econometric Models and Cross-spectral Methods
authors: Granger, C. W. J.
notes: The baseline definition (causality as incremental predictability conditional on history). Included to make one thing explicit that the registry leaves implicit: the AIEF-1.3 design is NOT a Granger test. It intervenes on the mechanism and measures a downstream structural difference. That is a stronger identification strategy than incremental predictability, and the claim should say so instead of leaving 'causal' undefined.

title: Detecting Causality in Complex Ecosystems
authors: Sugihara, G.; May, R.; Ye, H.; Hsieh, C.-H.; Deyle, E.; Fogarty, M.; Munch, S.
notes: The constructive critique of Granger for coupled dynamical systems. Cited because it establishes that predictability-based causal inference is contested for precisely the class of system AIEF studies (strongly coupled, state-dependent, nonseparable) - which strengthens the case for an intervention design over any observational causal metric. Together with LIT-0023 this pins the two poles the AIEF design sits between.

title: Measuring Information Transfer
authors: Schreiber, T.
notes: The most directly relevant find of Round 2 for claim design. EMP-AIEF14-02's matched-phase ablation exists precisely because a naive comparison cannot separate history that is genuinely transmitted from history that both conditions merely share. Schreiber names that confound - 'shared information due to common history' - and gives the conditioning remedy. The matched-phase design is the same logic applied to an intervention instead of to an estimator. This supplies the formal reason the design is necessary, which the registry currently asserts only empirically.

title: Bootstrap-Based Improvements for Inference with Clustered Errors
authors: Cameron, A. C.; Gelbach, J. B.; Miller, D. L.
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
notes: HONESTY NOTE: the bibliographic record was confirmed, but this paper's abstract was not read directly. The description of its contribution used here is taken second-hand from LIT-0002 (the 2015 practitioner's guide by Cameron & Miller), which states that in Monte Carlos with few clusters the cluster bootstrap did not eliminate over-rejection, and that the authors proposed the wild cluster bootstrap, which holds the regressors fixed across bootstrap replications. A Round 3 task is to read the original abstract and remove this dependency.

title: Reworking Wild Bootstrap Based Inference For Clustered Errors
authors: Webb, M. D.
notes: Sets the threshold that decides whether EMP-AIEF13-01's interval needs remedial work. N=100 (disjoint cohort) and N=40 (the rejected cohort) both exceed Webb's eleven-cluster threshold, so neither needs the 6-point distribution. Round 2 therefore reports NO ACTION REQUIRED on the interval construction - a clean negative result. Year attribution varies across citing works and the RePEc record lists a 2014-11 revision; a journal version appeared in 2023. Recorded as 2013 with the ambiguity noted rather than resolved by preference.

title: Phase oscillator networks with multiple and state-dependent delays: A framework for exploring white matter plasticity in neurodynamics
authors: Jolly, G.; Nicks, R.; Ruschel, S.; Iskenderoglu, G.; Coombes, S.
notes: The most important CAUTION of Round 2. Stated by a group actively working this exact problem: phase reduction LOSES delay information. Any AIEF claim that describes delay effects through a phase variable inherits that loss. The AIEF-1.4 programme keeps the delay explicit - which is the 'less restrictive approach' this paper recommends - so this is simultaneously a constraint and a point in the repository's favour that should be stated rather than left implicit. Shared authorship with LIT-0016 (Ruschel, Nicks, Coombes) confirms a fast-moving group on this mechanism.

title: Numerical Methods for Delay Differential Equations
authors: Bellen, A.; Zennaro, M.
venue: Numerical Mathematics and Scientific Computation, Oxford University Press
notes: The canonical reference for DDE numerics, and the source of the caveat that matters most for AIEF_1_4_SPLIT_STATE_ABLATION. In a DDE the state is the history segment (LIT-0010), and a well-posed DDE needs an explicit history function on the initial interval. Two consequences for the split-state design. (1) An ablation applied at the split time does not merely reset a component; it injects a first-order discontinuity into the history, and the method-of-steps error analysis is organised around how such discontinuities propagate and smooth. (2) Comparing post-split trajectories across arms therefore compares two different discontinuity structures unless the split is handled identically in both. The registry currently records the split operation but not this propagation effect. Round 4/5 action item: state the discontinuity order induced by the split and confirm it is identical across arms.

title: Synchronization in oscillator networks with delayed coupling: A stability criterion
authors: Earl, M. G.; Strogatz, S. H.
notes:
HONESTY NOTE: this record is VERIFIED_METADATA for the bibliographic fields, but the description of the content is taken from how the delay-coupled-oscillator literature consistently cites it (verified across four independent citing works in the same search), not from the paper's own abstract. A Round 4 task is to open the abstract and tighten this.

Why it matters: it gives REJ-LOCK-03 a published alternative. The rejected claim was that mature oscillator frequencies satisfy the bare algebraic zero-sum omega_i + G_i = 0. For delay-coupled networks the correct object is the phase-locked condition: frequency and phase offsets satisfy implicit equations in the delay, so an algebraic sum is the wrong functional form regardless of numerics. Combined with LIT-0018 and LIT-0028 this turns a bare negative numerical result into a structural statement.

title: From Kuramoto to Crawford: exploring the onset of synchronization in populations of coupled oscillators
authors: Strogatz, S. H.
notes: Resolves LEAD-0004. Context only: it does not adjudicate any AIEF claim and is not offered as support for one. Its value is that it defines the vocabulary (order parameter, critical coupling, phase-locked versus incoherent) that the AIEF-1.0-1.2 adaptive-network material uses without citing. Useful when the Era-1 provenance gap (see ROUND_03 F16) is repaired: whichever code produced those results was working in this framework and should say so.

title: Wild Bootstrap Inference for Wildly Different Cluster Sizes
authors: MacKinnon, J. G.; Webb, M. D.
notes: Resolves LEAD-0005 (the Queen's working paper 1314 became this journal article). Confirms and sharpens Round 2's F14 without changing it. The failure modes named here are unbalanced cluster sizes and few TREATED clusters. Neither applies to the AIEF design: seeds are exchangeable and every seed is treated in every arm, so the treated fraction is 1 by construction and cluster sizes are equal. Conclusion stands: no remedial work on EMP-AIEF13-01's interval. The one transferable caution is that if a future design ever ablates a SUBSET of seeds, this paper says the interval construction must change at that moment.

title: Reachability for Nonsmooth Systems with Lexicographic Jacobians
authors: Ji, C.; Zhang, H.; Mitra, S.
venue: Tools and Algorithms for the Construction and Analysis of Systems (TACAS 2025), LNCS, pp. 364-384
notes: Resolves LEAD-0006, and is the applied demonstration Round 2 wanted. It is the same structural situation as the CF block: a nonsmooth map, a Jacobian that does not exist at the non-differentiable points, and the choice between hybridizing into smooth modes or using the lexicographic derivative. The authors do the latter and report a 50% accuracy gain over hybridization. Two implications for AIEF. (1) CF03's approach is current best practice in a verified-systems venue, not a local convention. (2) The 'hybridize into modes' alternative is precisely the branch bookkeeping that the AIEF audit performs when it tracks winner signatures, and this paper is evidence that the bookkeeping is avoidable rather than necessary. Worth citing if the CF block is ever rewritten.
